evidence.claim: Convatec evaluated its next-generation multi-layered foam dressing, ConvaFoam, in a prospective, multicentre, open-label clinical trial (NCT05632276) published in the Journal of Wound Care, which demonstrated excellent exudate management and a maximum seven-day wear time in indicated surgical and traumatic wounds.

Convatec announced results from a randomized controlled clinical trial demonstrating that its AQUACEL Ag+ Extra antimicrobial and antibiofilm wound dressing, powered by its proprietary Hydrofiber technology, achieved a 74.8% complete healing rate for venous leg ulcers at 12 weeks compared to 55.6% for the standard of care.

Convatec received U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance on 26 October 2018 for its Avelle NPWT system, a canister-less, portable system that delivers a fixed negative pressure of 80 mmHg (± 20 mmHg) and features a disposable pump with a 30-day operating lifetime.

In a prospective clinical evaluation (the SPACE Study) published on PubMed, the Avelle NPWT system achieved a 46.8% reduction in mean wound area (decreasing from 13.4 cm² to 7.3 cm²) by Day 13 across 59 patients with hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers.

The company reports that its product InnovaMatrix AC is an FDA-cleared porcine placental-derived extracellular matrix medical device cleared under a 510(k) license for 15 separate medical indications, including the management of partial and full-thickness wounds, pressure ulcers, venous ulcers, diabetic ulcers, and second-degree burns.

Convatec announced that it secured European CE mark and UKCA mark regulatory approval on September 22, 2025, for ConvaMatrix, a single-use porcine placenta-derived extracellular collagen matrix skin substitute designed to treat hard-to-heal venous leg and diabetic foot ulcers.
